title: ExceptionalProEtaleRealization
statement: Realize the pro-etale quotient modules of [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image] in the same explicit finite scalar coordinates as [def-pur-adic-etale-realization]. This is an additive exact equivalence. Its comparison with intrinsic finite realization is uniquely fixed on all scalar-unit sections. Derive it by exact localization. The strict coefficient-coordinate functor commutes with ordinary evaluation as an equality of functors. Identify every normalized derived evaluation package with exact derived evaluation by its factorization square on all complexes. Compose these maps and the actual coordinate-equivalence counit to define the direct and inverse coordinate/evaluation identifications.

proof.text: Restriction of scalars along a ring-sheaf isomorphism is an equivalence: construct the inverse from its inverse ring map, with identity-on-section unit and counit. Apply the constant-ring module-sheaf equivalence and fixed-ring scalar restriction along the explicit quotient equivalence. The composite is an equivalence, hence preserves finite limits and colimits and is additive. The same ring-sheaf argument gives integralExceptionalLevel_equivalence.

The constantRingScalar calculation identifies the constant-ring presentation map on a constant scalar. Naturality of ring sheafification and the quotient equivalence inverse equation then identify the composite scalar map with the intrinsic scalar unit. Consequently the intrinsic module-sheafification unit defines a linear natural transformation from the identity to realization followed by the two coordinate restrictions. Its components are bijections: the underlying abelian presheaf is already a sheaf, so its sheafification unit is invertible. Invert this natural transformation to obtain the normalized fixed-unit comparison. Surjectivity of scalar-unit sections proves uniqueness.

Precomposition with the intrinsic realization equivalence is fully faithful on functor categories. Lift the composite of the fixed-unit comparison with the equivalence unit through this fully faithful functor. Cancelling the equivalence unit proves its normalization and uniqueness. Apply exact derived localization to this actual ordinary comparison.

The strict coordinate functor and ordinary evaluation commute definitionally, both on objects and on maps. For a normalized evaluation package, lift its factorization isomorphism composed with the inverse exact factorization through quasi-isomorphism localization. The lift component formula proves the required square. Cancel the exact factorization isomorphism and use localization natural-transformation extensionality to prove uniqueness. Compose these specified comparisons and the actual coordinate-equivalence counit exactly as in the existing direct and inverse coordinate definitions.
